idea-plugin.name: Claude Terminal Tab Persistence
idea-plugin.description:
Claude Terminal Tab Persistence for Rider / IntelliJ

Auto-restores your Claude Code terminal sessions across IDE restarts. The plugin tracks alive Claude sessions in ~/.claude/rider-plugin/active-sessions/ and, on next project open, spawns one fresh terminal tab per saved session running claude --resume <sid>.

2.0 redesign

Ground-up rework. Earlier versions tried to coordinate tab titles with one-shot writes, which lost races and left tabs as "Local". The new model:

  • The plugin owns Claude tab titles. Every tab hosting a Claude session shows ✳ <name>, and the glyph animates while the session is thinking (mirroring Claude's own busy/idle status). Titles are continuously enforced — a tab clobbered to "Local" self-heals within half a second.
  • Names that stick. Display name priority: your explicit name (Rider's "Rename Tab" or /tab) > Claude's auto-generated topic name > the cached topic. Renames are adopted and persisted across restarts, never fought.
  • One file per alive session. active-sessions/<sid>.json — race-safe, no per-project file conflicts.
  • Bounded eviction backlog. session-backlog.json keeps the last 50 evicted sessions so you can recover them with /tabs-history.

Slash Commands

  • /tab — set this session's tab name explicitly (persists across restarts)
  • /tabs-status — live sessions + recent eviction backlog for the current project
  • /tabs-backup — explicit sync: write per-sid files for every alive Claude process
  • /tabs-history — browse the eviction backlog and print a resume command
  • /tabs-restore — list current per-sid files and print resume commands
  • /tabs-clear — clear active-sessions/ for the current project

Requirements: Rider / IntelliJ 2026.1+, Claude Code CLI, Node.js (for the bundled helper scripts).

Coexists with the JetBrains AI Assistant chat tool window (AI Agents panel: Junie / Claude Agent / Codex) and Anthropic's official Claude Code [Beta] plugin. This plugin manages terminal-launched Claude CLI sessions only — chat tabs in the AI Agents panel are managed by JetBrains.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.0.0 — Ground-up rework: per-session tracking, title ownership, thinking animation

Crash & restore reliability

  • Durable (fsync) writes — a hard crash can no longer zero saved session files.
  • A session is only ever deleted on an explicit tab close; window/IDE-close and unconfirmed deaths demote to restore-pending instead.
  • Tabs restore in their saved left-to-right order.
  • No duplicate or empty ghost tabs on slow resumes; sturdier tab→session matching.
  • Backlog cap raised to 100.

Title ownership: ✳ name + thinking animation

  • The plugin owns Claude tab titles and drives the animation. A title controller enforces ✳ <name> on every tab hosting a Claude session (~450ms tick) and cycles the glyph (✳ ✶ ✷ ✸) while the session's own status says busy. Rationale: the native CLI animation lives in the terminal's application title, which a custom tab name hides and which some shells swallow — per-tab names and native animation are mutually exclusive, so the plugin provides both itself. A tab clobbered to "Local" self-heals within one tick; this replaces the one-shot title writes that lost races and left restored tabs unnamed.
  • Names from Claude's own metadata. Claude Code maintains an auto-generated topic name per session; the plugin mirrors it (prettified) as the default display name. User-started tabs are matched by process ancestry and titled the same way.
  • Renames are adopted, not fought. Rename a tab in Rider (or run /tab My Name in the session) and that text becomes the persistent userName — it outranks the auto topic, survives restarts, and keeps the glyph + animation around it.
  • Single lifecycle owner. /tabs-backup is purely additive now (registers/refreshes live sessions, never deletes); only the plugin evicts, demotes, or backlogs entries. A user-closed tab is moved to the backlog immediately with its names, so an accidental close is always recoverable via /tabs-history.

Survive Rider restarts: observed vs unobserved deaths

  • Fixes "nothing restores after a Rider restart." When Rider exits, every Claude process dies with it. On the next start the poll loop saw all recorded pids dead and evicted the entire saved state to the backlog before the restore loops ran (one window's poll raced another window's restore and won by 2 seconds). The eviction contract is now "evict deaths we OBSERVED": a one-shot startup reconcile rewrites every dead-pid entry to pid=null (restore-pending, never evicted), so only sessions that die while the plugin is actually watching get evicted.
  • Strike spacing. The dead-strike tracker is shared across project windows in one Rider JVM; two windows polling milliseconds apart could burn both K=2 strikes in one logical round. Strikes now require ≥4s spacing to count.
  • Named from the first frame. Restored tabs are created with their composed ✳ <saved name> title (user name > cached topic > "Claude"), then the title controller keeps it correct — "Local" can no longer appear, even transiently.

Spawn-attempt cap + sibling-project arbitration

  • Hard cap of 3 spawn attempts per sid per Rider session. 2.0.1's retry-spawn had no ceiling — a resume that consistently failed to register an alive Claude (e.g. the CLI's large-session "resume from summary?" confirmation prompt holding the process pre-registration) spawned a new terminal tab every 60 seconds, without bound. After 3 attempts the entry stays in active-sessions/ for manual recovery and a warning lands in idea.log.
  • Sibling-project arbitration. The worktree clause (<base>-<suffix>) no longer lets a parent project's window claim a sibling project's sessions (e.g. MyApp claiming MyApp-mobile). A dash-suffix cwd is claimed only when no more-specific project base is known, where "known" = any open Rider project + every entry in project-index.json (projects seen open before). Genuine git worktrees are never opened as their own Rider projects, so the parent still claims them; sibling projects wait for their own window.
  • project-index.json maintenance restored (dropped in the 2.0 rewrite; needed by the arbitration above and the /tabs-status fast path).

Migration-spawn safety net

  • pid=null entries never auto-evict. 2.0's migration seeds active-sessions/ with pid=null until the first poll confirms a matching alive Claude. If the on-restore spawn didn't materialise within two polls (Terminal tool window not ready, etc.), the dead-strike logic was evicting the migration seed to the backlog before the user ever saw a tab. Now pid=null entries are skipped by the eviction path entirely — they sit until either confirmed alive or the user explicitly clears via /tabs-clear.
  • Retry-spawn on every poll. If an unconfirmed entry's cwd belongs to this project and we haven't already spawned for its sid in this Rider session, the next poll re-attempts claude --resume in a fresh terminal tab. Dedup is via an in-memory attemptedRestoreSpawnSids set so a successful first spawn isn't re-fired.

Storage model: per-sid files + bounded backlog

  • Tab titles are no longer managed by the plugin. Rider's defaults ("Local", "Local (2)") win. Use Rider's native "Rename Tab" if you want a label — Rider persists it. Rationale: 1.x's naming layer was the proximate cause of every recurring bug — rename storms thrashing the restore file, cross-project session pollution, sessions evicted by transient detection misses, two tabs cross-wired to the same sid.
  • Per-sid storage. One file per alive Claude session under ~/.claude/rider-plugin/active-sessions/<sid>.json instead of one per-project restore-<hash>.json. Race-safe across multiple Rider windows (atomic tmp+rename), idempotent writes, filtering moved to read-time.
  • Eviction backlog. ~/.claude/rider-plugin/session-backlog.json — global, max 50 entries, newest first, prepended on each eviction with dedup-by-sid. Browse via /tabs-history.
  • K=2 dead-strike eviction. A per-sid file is deleted only after two consecutive polls confirm the underlying Claude process is gone (PID file missing OR PID file's sessionId differs from ours). Forgives transient detection misses without keeping zombies past ~10s.
  • Worktree-sibling cwd tolerance. A session whose cwd is <projectBase>-<suffix> (typical git worktree shape) is recognised as belonging to the parent project. Fixes the original bug where D:\Dev\MyApp-feature sessions inside an MyApp Rider window were rejected by the cwd filter.
  • One-time migration from 1.x. First 2.0 launch reads every existing restore-<hash>.json, seeds active-sessions/ with pid=null entries (first poll either confirms or starts the dead-strike counter), and renames legacy files to .pre-2.0 siblings. Old names.json is preserved as names.json.pre-2.0 (its content isn't merged — restore-file tabName is more recent).
  • /tab simplified. Now a "force-save now" command. $ARGUMENTS becomes an optional metaName note shown in /tabs-status listings — never used as a tab title.
  • /tabs-backup rewritten. Explicit sync: scans ~/.claude/sessions/ and writes per-sid files for every alive Claude, evicting dead per-sid files (no K-strike grace — immediate). Reports synced: N added, M evicted, K already current.
  • ~65% net code reduction. ClaudeTabWatcherStartup.kt 3200 → ~600 lines; ClaudeTabsStorage.kt 615 → ~150 lines. Deleted: SpawnedWidgetRenameFastPath.kt, ImmediateRenamePersistence.kt, the rename-application chain (renameTab, findTerminalTitle, installTitleListener, watchTabsDirectory, handlePidRename, handleTermSessionRename, persistRenameImmediately, handleRename), the canonicalSessionIdFor 3-strategy resolver, claimedByTabWalk cross-project arbitration, sessionAliases rotated→canonical mirroring, and the entire names.json store.
  • Bundled scripts pruned. Removed: rename-tab.sh, session-start-hook.sh, tab.sh, tab-backup.js. Added: tab-now.js (immediate per-sid write for the new /tab). Kept: current-project.js, backup-active.js (rewritten).

1.0.18

  • Window-state serialization, worktree-resume transcript lookup, DockManager-based 5th tab source, cross-project arbitration, canonical-id cache correction, names.json auto-apply, two-poll-grace eviction, authoritative saveState with name preservation. Superseded by the 2.0 redesign.
